claims.claim: The company’s core business is built around low‑price, limited‑selection warehouses and e‑commerce sites that rely on high sales volume and rapid inventory turnover to sustain profitability at lower gross margins.
claims.quote: We operate membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover.

claims.claim: The strategy emphasizes a very narrow SKU count per warehouse—under four thousand active items—compared with broader retailers, and a broader online assortment of nine‑to‑eleven thousand SKUs.
claims.quote: We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business, significantly less than other broadline retailers. We average from 9,000 to 11,000 SKUs online, some of which are available in our warehouses.

claims.claim: The firm competes globally with a wide range of retailers, including big‑box chains, online platforms, gasoline stations and other warehouse clubs such as Sam’s Club and BJ’s.
claims.quote: We compete on a worldwide basis with global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers, including supermarkets, supercenters, online retailers, gasoline stations, hard discounters, department and specialty stores, and operators selling a single category or narrow range of merchandise. Walmart, Target, Kroger, and Amazon are among our significant general merchandise retail competitors in the U.S. We also compete with other warehouse clubs, including Walmart’s Sam’s Club and BJ’s Wholesale Club in the U.S.

claims.claim: The company’s private‑label brand, Kirkland Signature, is positioned as high‑quality yet lower‑priced than national brands and is expected to expand its sales penetration.
claims.quote: We believe that Kirkland Signature products are high quality, offered at prices that are generally lower than national brands, and help lower costs, differentiate our merchandise offerings, and generally earn higher margins. We expect to continue to increase the sales penetration of our private-label items.

claims.claim: Membership fee revenue grew eleven percent in the fiscal year, driven by new sign‑ups, fee increases and upgrades to the Executive tier.
claims.quote: Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907, driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive membership;

claims.claim: Digital‑enabled comparable sales rose roughly twenty percent year‑over‑year, reflecting strong e‑commerce and mobile engagement.
The company intends to continue opening warehouses in new and existing markets, acknowledging that new locations can take time to become profitable and may cannibalize existing sales.
claims.quote: We also achieve net sales growth by opening new warehouses. As our warehouse base grows… Negative aspects of such growth include lower initial operating profitability… and cannibalization of sales at existing warehouses when openings occur in existing markets.

claims.claim: Gasoline sales, representing about eleven percent of total net sales in 2026, are leveraged to increase warehouse traffic while contributing a lower gross‑margin percentage.
claims.quote: Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026.

claims.claim: In the fourth quarter, net income was boosted by a non‑recurring benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, adding $0.15 per diluted share after accounting for partial reinvestment of the refunds.
claims.quote: This year's fourth quarter was positively impacted by a non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, less partial reinvestment of those refunds in increased member values.

claims.claim: The company reported net sales growth of ten point one percent for the fiscal year, reaching $297.2 billion, and comparable sales growth of six point six percent company‑wide.
claims.quote: Net sales for the fiscal year increased 10.1 percent, to $297.2 billion, from $269.9 billion last year.

The filing mentions risk factors related to cyber‑security without detailing any specific upcoming security initiatives, leaving a gap for a claim about a planned major cybersecurity platform rollout.
